title: Metrics: time to fix, scan coverage and security debt

videos.script: Your pipeline now finds things. Over a year, across four teams, it finds hundreds of them. {{count}} The first number anybody reports is the count. It is also the least useful one. It rises when you scan more, and falls when you stop looking. This lesson is about the numbers that answer real questions. {{ttr}} How fast do we fix what we find? For that, the median beats the mean, and you will see why in one table. {{coverage}} Where are we blind? A repository nothing scans has no findings, so a dashboard shows it as clean. {{debt}} What is waiting? Open findings, sorted by age, and the ones past the date we promised. You will generate a year of findings with a short program, the same on every run, and measure it with a second one. {{goodhart}} Then you will find a team whose numbers look the best in the company. They are the best because of what that team chose to count. That is Goodhart's law, and the last part of the lesson is how to report numbers it cannot bend. {{report}}
